questions.text: I tend to take jokes and comments literally when others see layers of meaning.
I prefer that the group collectively decides when a meeting has run its course.
My emotional responses have a muted quality compared to what I observe in others.
I routinely hand off leads, clients, or referrals to colleagues who need them more.
I notice when someone volunteers to leave a room to give others privacy they did not explicitly request.
I'm comfortable with ambiguity in group projects and trust things will sort themselves out.
When I encounter injustice, my entire body lights up with agitation.
I routinely check in on neighbors, acquaintances, and distant friends to make sure they are okay.
I do not usually sense when the mood of a text conversation shifts because of an emoji choice or its absence.
I believe that the time I spend alone working on my goals is among my most valuable hours.
I feel uneasy when I don't have a clear plan for the week ahead.
I am the type of person who always has a five-year plan or long-range vision.
I want to support whoever launches new ventures within my team.
I feel most alive when I am steering the course of a project.
I rarely notice the implicit choreography of how a group arranges itself when it walks together.
I tend to move through emotionally charged moments with a sense of groundedness.
When I have extra money, my first thought is who else could use it.
Understanding how many people a problem harms makes me want to see their suffering reduced.
I return borrowed items promptly because outstanding obligations weigh on me.
I prefer to own the outcome of a decision rather than share that ownership.
Wanting others to suffer less is a real motivation in my life.
I detect when someone answers a different question than the one that was asked to steer the conversation.
I experience the pressure of a deadline not just mentally but as a tightening sensation throughout my body.
I tend to frame every major decision by asking: does this move me closer to where I want to be?
I am the one who typically helps the group settle on the key question together.
Even when someone I am with is clearly in distress, their pain leaves me largely unmoved.
When someone shares their struggle with me, I experience it as a call to action rather than as information.
I think of each day as its own self-contained experience rather than an investment in the future.
I am easily swept up in the emotional energy of a crowd or a room.
I often sense that there is a conversation happening beneath the surface conversation.
Others' suffering sometimes fails to register as something that matters to me.
I feel that personal reading time is a non-negotiable part of my schedule.
I experience the act of letting go of something as a natural, uncomplicated process.
I make choices based on present circumstances and adapt to downstream effects as they appear.
When a person I know is struggling, I rarely feel a wish to be of help.
I naturally assume the authority to speak on behalf of a group.
